Cause: PERSONAL_BEST (h06ForbiddenClaims.test.ts L108-113: `(?:new|current|…) best`, `best (?:so far|yet)`, `best (?:\w+ )?(?:today|so far|yet|…)`) was written for player-progress copy but is applied as an allow-list inside a ±ALLOW_WINDOW slice around any 'best' match, so 'new best-in-class' and 'best <word> today/yet/so far' are exempt even when the subject is the product.
breaks.title: PERSONAL_BEST allow-window lets product superlatives through ('Best app today', 'Our best analyzer yet', 'The best coach so far', 'best-in-class')

breaks.expected: Any percentage attached to a correctness claim about the analysis is an accuracy-% claim under APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md and must be reported.
breaks.observed: No [accuracy-percentage] report for 'Gets your form right 95% of the time', 'Spot-on 98% of the time', 'Nails it 99% of the time'; control 'Accurate 95% of the time' IS reported and 'Right 9 times out of 10 swings' IS reported. Cause: the PERCENT branch of the accuracy rule only pairs a percentage with the ACCURACY_WORD list (accura*, precis*, correct*, …), not with correctness synonyms (right, spot-on, nails it, gets it).
breaks.title: Accuracy percentages phrased as correctness ('right 95% of the time', 'spot-on 98% of the time', 'nails it 99% of the time') are not reported

breaks.expected: JSON (and any other Metro-bundled text module) under apps/mobile/src and the bundled @pickle/* packages is part of 'all user-facing strings' and must be scanned.
breaks.observed: A screen doing `import copy from './copy.json'` and rendering `<Text>{copy.badge}</Text>` with copy.json = {"badge":"Live Court","tagline":"Also on Google Play"} produces no report: `sourceFiles()` only collects .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx and unresolved member access becomes `{…}`. Metro bundles .json modules, so this copy ships verbatim.
breaks.repro: cd apps/mobile && npx jest --ci __tests__/attackH06ForbiddenClaimsBypass.test.ts -t 'JSON copy table'
breaks.title: Copy the Metro bundle ships from imported JSON is outside the corpus

breaks.expected: Every user-visible plist string (usage descriptions, display/bundle name, UIApplicationShortcutItems titles/subtitles, UTType descriptions) is scanned regardless of intervening comments/whitespace.
breaks.observed: `UIApplicationShortcutItemTitle` = 'Live Court' (home-screen quick action, user-visible) is not reported; `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` whose <string> is separated from its <key> by an XML comment is not reported (regex `<key>…</key>\s*<string>`), while the adjacent control usage description is reported.
breaks.title: Info.plist scan is limited to *UsageDescription/CFBundleDisplayName with an adjacent <string>; quick-action titles and comment-separated entries are missed

breaks.expected: The operator-typed value belonging to an ENTER: marker is scanned in full, including wrapped/continuation lines and escaped pipes in table cells.
breaks.observed: In docs/APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md, `- Promotional text — \`ENTER:\`` followed by the value on the next indented line ('… Now with Live Court.') is not reported; the wrapped second line of an ENTER bullet ('the DUPR-style estimate is disclaimed.') is not reported; a table cell `\`ENTER:\` Best pickleball coach \| Android tagline` is reported only as 'Best pickleball coach \\' — the text after the escaped pipe (Android) is dropped. Control backticked ENTER value on the marker line is reported. Cause: `enterValues()` only reads the marker's own line and splits on the first '|' without honouring '\|'.
breaks.title: Dossier ENTER: extraction misses values on continuation lines and truncates cells at an escaped pipe

breaks.expected: Either resolve these assembly shapes or document them as out of scope; today the comment claims 'concatenations' are handled.
breaks.observed: `let store = 'Google '; store += 'Play'` and `'Live '.concat('Court')` rendered in <Text> are not reported; Swift `"Google " + "Play"` and `"\(brand) Play exclusive"` (brand = "Google") are not reported. Controls `'Google ' + 'Play'` (TS) and the plain Swift literal are reported.
breaks.title: Phrases assembled with `+=`, `.concat()`, Swift `+` or Swift interpolation are scanned only as their innocuous halves

breaks.expected: Given the candidate explicitly hardens against invisible/format characters, confusable letters (at least Cyrillic/Greek Latin look-alikes) should be folded or flagged as suspicious mixed-script copy.
breaks.observed: '\u0410ndroid users: coming soon', 'Also on G\u043E\u043Egle Play', 'Live C\u043Eurt mode', 'Compare with your DU\u0420R rating' are not reported (NFKC does not fold Cyrillic А/о/Р to Latin); control zero-width-space split 'Google\u200BPlay' IS reported.
breaks.title: Cyrillic homoglyphs survive NFKC normalization and bypass every term rule

breaks.expected: APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md forbids superlatives, AI-coach-equivalence and guest-entry copy as categories, not just the enumerated words; at minimum top/top-tier/unbeaten/outperforms/elite/pinpoint, 'smarter than/beats … coach', 'artificial intelligence coach', and 'continue as a visitor' should be covered.
breaks.observed: Not reported in rendered <Text>: 'The top pickleball coaching app', 'Top-tier analysis', 'Unbeaten pickleball analysis', 'Outperforms every other pickleball app', 'Professional-grade analysis', 'Elite accuracy', 'Pinpoint accuracy on every swing', 'Never misses a swing', 'Smarter than any coach', 'Beats a real coach', 'An artificial intelligence coach in your phone', 'Continue as a visitor', 'Try it first, sign in later'. Control 'Better than a coach' IS reported ([ai-coach-equivalence]).
breaks.title: Rule vocabulary gaps: common superlative / coach-equivalence / guest-entry phrasings pass
